item.title: UK police open sex offence probe into comedian and author David Walliams
item.description:
Parents take action while several independent bookshops say they had already stopped stocking his titles In Sarah’s house, David Walliams has been a bedtime staple for years. Her children, aged eight, six and four, have dressed up as his characters for World Book Day – they love the over-the-top, unusual names and illustrations. Now, all the books are going. “I’ll probably take them away and replace them with other authors,” says Sarah, a mother in west London. “Sooner rather than later, so they don’t realise.” If any of her children ask why, she will tell them “that his choices aren’t great and that I think we should be reading other books”. item.title: IRGC says tanker caught fire after hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
First direct attack on US military installations for months was in response to US airstrike on communications tower Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it has targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik overlooking the strait of Hormuz. It is Iran’s first direct attack on US military installations for months. “This is a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end its aerial mischief and oil smuggling in the strait of Hormuz,” the IRGC said. “In the event of repeated violations and aggression, the IRGC aerospace force is on full alert to confront the enemy without constraint.” Continue reading...

item.title: Democrats fumbled the Hegseth impeachment. That could be a blessing in disguise | Claire Finkelstein
item.description:
Most of America bemoans political gridlock in the nation’s capital. DC area commuters deplore the city’s transit gridlock. But Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth may now be a fan of DC’s legendary traffic snarls. It appears that crosstown traffic may have prevented him from becoming only the third Cabinet secretary ever impeached by the House of Representatives. The House voted 211-204 this week to divert an effort by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) to impeach Hegseth. House Republicans moved to block a straight, up-or-down vote on impeachment. Instead, Republicans forced a vote on sending the articles to the Judiciary Committee. That’s where they’d go to die. If the House failed to sidetrack the articles, Members would have then voted on actual impeachment. If a simple majority voted to impeach, Hegseth would join 19th century Secretary of War William Belknap and former Homeland Security Secretary…

item.title: 'We just ran' - One killed, four injured in shooting near Washington DC gym
item.description:
Earlier this week, police in the city of Tustin, California received a report of a drive-by shooting at Flight at Tustin Legacy, the office campus that plays host to Wasteland and Clockwork Revolution developer inXile, among other businesses. Fortunately, no one was hurt, but inXile is now “working closely” with local authorities amid an ongoing investigation. item.title: Brooks and Marcus on how Republicans are responding to midterm losses
item.description:
After the shellacking Republicans just took in the midterm elections, a common refrain among conservatives is that we should all be terrified of what comes next. Whether you get your commentary from X, Instagram, or friends on Facebook, you may have heard fear that the Democrats will vastly expand the size and scope of government, usher in socialism, or destroy Western civilization. There is no doubt that a lot of bad, big-government policies are in store. But if the prospect of Democrats returning to power is so terrifying, why on earth did Republicans elect a president and vice president as controversial as Donald Trump and J.D. Vance? Why did they support so many policies in clear opposition to the promotion of a free and virtuous society? Did they think a majority of voters would enjoy the result?
